concept: ASP DLQ document schema versus processor-level failures

claims.text: The documented non-retryable processor failures include StreamProcessorWorkerOutOfMemory (418), when the pipeline exceeds tier memory limits, and StreamProcessorInvalidOptions (420), for invalid pipeline syntax or configuration. These failures immediately fail the processor; a configured DLQ does not turn them into document-level rejection records. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

For retryable user errors, Atlas Stream Processing attempts processor restarts a limited number of times over five minutes, then enters FAILED if the attempts fail. Invalid credentials, external connectivity, and permissions are documented user-error examples. Internal system errors instead receive retries without a time limit and engineering alerts. These are processor recovery policies, not promises that failed documents will be written to the DLQ. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

The $https onError choice applies to HTTP responses 400, 404, 410, 413, 414, and 431. All 2XX responses count as success; any other HTTP status is treated as fail. The documented example is HTTP 500, which stops the processor despite the default onError: dlq setting. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The meaning of ignore differs between stages: $https passes the affected document onward, whereas $externalFunction discards it according to the operations guide. Both stages default to dlq, and fail stops the processor even when a DLQ is configured. A common onError field name does not imply identical document disposition. For $https, ignore can therefore forward the affected document without a corresponding DLQ entry. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The $externalFunction behavior section documents an override of its onError setting: if the pipeline cannot convert the document to proper JSON, or its final payload stage does not produce a valid BSON object, the document goes to the DLQ regardless of onError. This exception prevents treating fail or ignore as unconditional routing rules for every failure in that stage. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

$externalFunction configuration errors, including invalid expressions, bypass onError and fail the processor. Setting as with execution:"async" returns an error; parallelism greater than one requires execution:"sync". (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Baseline syntax correction: $validate.validationAction accepts "discard" (default, no DLQ write) or "dlq". The reference describes "dlq" as logging the violation and performing best-effort discard without transactional guarantees. Existing warn/error advice is not the documented stream-stage contract. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Invalid pipeline syntax or configuration and internal system errors do not create DLQ records. Diagnose those processor errors through the separate error-handling policy rather than assuming DLQ routing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Incorrect $https operator configuration, such as invalid expressions, does not invoke onError. Separately, a header-value expression that fails or produces a non-string sends the document to DLQ without issuing the request; invalid HTTP header names or values are ignored. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For asynchronous $externalFunction calls, onError handles AWS API errors but does not handle Lambda function errors. The pipeline continues without waiting for the function response; a configured ASP DLQ therefore does not establish capture of later asynchronous function failures. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Baseline schema correction: monitoring identifies processorName, dlqTime.$date, operatorName, errInfo.reason, doc, and _stream_meta as always present. instanceName appears only for projects with multiple workspaces. These documented names replace the legacy universal originalDocument/errorMessage/errorCode/timestamp assumption. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
